cohort: 200 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies who delivered after 28 weeks of gestation and were diagnosed with umbilical cord abnormalities either antenatally or during and after delivery.
finding: Umbilical cord abnormalities are a significant stress factor for the fetus, frequently leading to adverse neonatal outcomes including NICU admission, early and late neonatal death, and stillbirth, with nuchal cord being the most common abnormality.
followup_time: up to 28 days post-birth (late neonatal death)
